posts.title: We used to play outside
posts.description: We used to be outside people. When I was a child, everyone in our neighborhood, and almost everywhere else in the country, was out playing on the streets. It was the norm, and if you weren’t out there, you were the odd one. After school, everyone would rush out and join the others. We played football (the real one, not the American), hopscotch, and lots of other games. We skated, rode our bicycles, and went on swings, slides, and see-saws. We had the most fun. Then the computers came. We got PCs and game consoles, and to be honest, we were resistant to them at first. I remember that for the first few months, or years, we still played a lot in the streets, having fun and making memories. But we got more and more interested in the computers. Sadly, we all ended up stuck at home, staring at monitors and wasting our childhood. I love computers. posts.title: The bear and the bomb
posts.description: I don’t remember where I saw this, but there was a post about asking AI to make a moral decision, and it compared the answers of different AI models. It made me think about how we, as humans, would make those decisions. Imagine a bear from an endangered species is chasing a man who might have a nuclear bomb attached to him. He’s running towards a crowded part of Berlin, and if he really has a bomb, he can blow up the whole city. If you do nothing, the bear may or may not reach him, and the bomb won’t detonate if the bear does. If he’s innocent and the bear catches him, he’ll die because of your choice. If the man is a terrorist and the bear catches him, then he’ll get what he deserves. If the bear doesn’t reach him and he’s a terrorist, millions will die. If you shoot the bear, it can’t reach him anymore, and he keeps running and makes it to the crowded part of Berlin.
